cse-2015-3-cs-13.approach: Insert the keys one at a time: each new key walks down from the root, going left when smaller and right when larger, and becomes a leaf where the walk falls off the tree. Then read off the deepest level.
cse-2015-3-cs-13.given: Insert, in order: $71, 65, 84, 69, 67, 83$ into an empty BST.

steps.title: Insert 71 — it becomes the root
steps.body: The tree is empty, so 71 is the root (level 0).

steps.title: Insert 65 and 84
steps.body:
$65 < 71$ → left child of 71.

$84 > 71$ → right child of 71. Both are on level 1.

steps.title: Insert 69
steps.body: $69 < 71$ → go left to 65; $69 > 65$ → right child of 65 (level 2).

steps.title: Insert 67
steps.body: $67 < 71$ → left to 65; $67 > 65$ → right to 69; $67 < 69$ → **left child of 69** (level 3).

steps.title: Read the levels
steps.body:
Level 0: 71 · Level 1: 65, 84 · Level 2: 69, 83 · Level 3: **67**.

The only node on the lowest level is 67, option (B).

optionAnalysis.reason: 65 is a child of the root (level 1).
67 follows 71 → 65 → 69 and lands on level 3, the deepest.
69 is on level 2; 67 hangs below it.
83 is on level 2, as the left child of 84.

cse-2015-3-cs-13.shortcut: Only keys between 65 and 71 travel past level 2: 69 and then 67, which must go below 69. So 67 is deepest.
pitfalls: Assuming the last key inserted (83) is the deepest — depth depends on the comparison path, not on insertion order.
cse-2015-3-cs-13.verification: An in-order traversal of the final tree gives $65, 67, 69, 71, 83, 84$ — sorted, so the tree is a valid BST.
